title: Widen WAL writer flush batch to 512 to cut residual wal_wait
configuration_cause: wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) still leaves wal_waiting_backends p95=1 and sync_average_ms=0.112ms; the writer-side flush batch is the only actionable knob in the wal_commit_path bundle not yet pushed to its safe high bound.
mechanism: The r014 bundle (commit_delay=0, commit_siblings=20, wal_writer_flush_after=256) was accepted with +18% paired log gain and reduced InsertTweet p95 by 15-33%, confirming that removing the fixed commit sleep and batching writer-side WAL flushes is the right mechanism. Residual wal_wait persists at p95=1 backend. commit_delay=0 and commit_siblings=20 are already at their safe extremes (window permanently inactive), so the only remaining amplitude is the writer flush batch. Doubling wal_writer_flush_after 256->512 (4MB) coalesces more background WAL writes per fsync without gating foreground commits, further reducing writer-side sync frequency and queueing.
query_effect: No plan change; commit-path only. InsertTweet commit latency should tighten modestly as writer-side fsyncs coalesce.
expected_tps_effect: Small positive: freeing residual WAL wait capacity on the commit path raises completed-transaction goodput by a fraction of a percent.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 and wal_waiting_backends p95 decrease; GetUserTweets unaffected.

predictions.rationale: Larger writer flush batch coalesces more WAL writes per fsync, reducing backends waiting on WAL.
Fewer, larger writer-side flushes lower mean sync time per WAL sync.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity for completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: If 256 already saturates writer batching, doubling to 512 yields no measurable change in wal_waiting_backends.p95 or sync_average_ms.
If residual wait is group-commit collection rather than writer batching, a small nonzero commit_delay would help more than a larger flush batch.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Pushes the only remaining actionable knob in the accepted wal_commit_path bundle to a larger safe amplitude, targeting the residual wal_wait anomaly that r014 left at p95=1 backend.

nodes.label: Larger writer-side WAL flush batch coalesces fsyncs

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Double from incumbent 256 to 512 (8kB units = 4MB), inside allowed [0,1024]; larger safe amplitude of the r014-supported writer-flush-batching mechanism.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: writer flush batch size; batches background WAL writes to coalesce fsyncs

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Unchanged at safe low bound 0; r014 confirmed removing the fixed commit sleep is correct.
Unchanged at safe high bound 20; keeps the zero window inactive.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit activation threshold; window never activates
